articles.headline: Lamar Jackson, Ravens not focusing on field conditions in Rio
articles.description: A day before the Ravens travel to Brazil to play the Cowboys, quarterback Lamar Jackson said he isn't focusing on the condition of the field at Maracanã Stadium.
articles.headlineJa: ラマー・ジャクソンとレイブンズ、リオのピッチコンディションには囚われず
articles.descriptionJa: レイブンズがカウボーイズとの試合のためにブラジルへ渡る前日、クォーターバック（QB）のラマー・ジャクソンは、マラカナン・スタジアムのグラウンド状態には特に意識を向けていないと語った。
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- A day before the Baltimore Ravens travel to Brazil, quarterback Lamar Jackson said he isn't focusing on the condition of the field at Maracanã Stadium.

"I believe the NFL does a great job at having their specialists go out there and look over the fields," Jackson said Wednesday. "I cannot worry about that. I just have to worry about getting us a dub in Brazil. [As for] the field, we have played on bad fields plenty of times, so I cannot really dwell on that."

On Sunday, Baltimore plays the Dallas Cowboys in the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro.

The concerns about the quality of the playing surface at Rio's Maracanã Stadium started last week when professional soccer players voiced complaints about their home stadium's grass field. On Monday, NFL field director Nick Pappas told ESPN that there are "no concerns right now" about the field conditions in Rio.

Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton has heard about the criticism about the playing surface.

"There is a lot of just, 'he said, she said,' kind of thing going on right now, so we will see," Hamilton said. "I know the players are the product in this league. As soon as we lose 'putting the players forward' is when we lose the league. I am sure the league knows that and they are doing their best to put us in the position to be safe. So, that is not really in the forefront of my mind right now."

This is the Ravens' first international game since 2023, when they beat the Tennessee Titans 24-16 in London. The Ravens spent the entire week in England to prepare for that game.

For this trip, the Ravens and Cowboys are both flying to Brazil on Thursday night and will arrive Friday, which is two days before the game. The reason Baltimore isn't leaving earlier is because it's only a one-hour time difference.

"I feel like the rhetoric around the game after it is done is who handled the travel and everything better," Hamilton said. "I think that just goes hand in hand on who is being more of a pro or not. That is something that I think we can thrive at. So, I'm excited."

articles.headline: Jets starting DT David Onyemata undergoes core muscle surgery
articles.description: Jets defensive tackle David Onyemata, a starter in the base defense, underwent core-muscle surgery and will be sidelined for several weeks.
articles.headlineJa: ジェッツの先発DTデビッド・オニエマタが体幹筋肉の手術を受ける
articles.descriptionJa: ジェッツの基本ディフェンスで先発を務めるディフェンシブタックル（DT）のデビッド・オニエマタが体幹筋肉の手術を受け、数週間の離脱となる見込み。
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets defensive tackle David Onyemata, a starter in the base defense, underwent core-muscle surgery and will be sidelined for several weeks.

Coach Aaron Glenn wouldn't rule him out for the remainder of the season, saying he expects the veteran run stuffer to return at some point.

"I would think so," Glenn said Wednesday.

Onyemata, 33, was injured in the Jets' 20-17 overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. The Jets signed him to a one-year, $10.5 million contract in free agency, expecting him to bolster their run defense and provide veteran leadership for a young roster.

In two games, Onyemata played 45 defensive snaps, with no tackles, no sacks and three quarterback pressures. Onyemata, who played previously for the New Orleans Saints and Atlanta Falcons, is in his 11th season.

Jowon Briggs likely will replace him in the base defense. It also could mean a bigger role for rookie Darrell Jackson Jr., a fourth-round pick from Florida State.

The Jets, who finished 25th in yards allowed in 2025, are No. 1 after two weeks despite key injuries on defense. Edge rusher Joseph Ossai (foot) has missed two games, while safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) has missed one. Ossai is "pretty close" to being ready, according to Glenn. Fitzpatrick, still not practicing, may need another week.

The Jets (1-1) travel to the Detroit Lions (1-1) on Sunday.

Wide receiver Arian Smith, a 2025 fourth-round pick, is gone for the season after tearing an ACL. He, too, was injured against the Packers. He had no receptions this season; he made the roster because of his ability as a gunner on special teams. He missed a tackle at the catch point on Skyy Moore's 63-yard punt return, but raced downfield and pushed Moore out of bounds at the Jets' 19-yard line in the fourth quarter. The Jets wound up holding the Packers to a field goal.

Both Smith and Onyemata were placed on injured reserve.

Another injury to watch: Tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) didn't practice, and his status for Sunday appears uncertain.

articles.headline: Sources: Bengals' Andrei Iosivas expected to miss 4-6 weeks
articles.description: Bengals wide receiver Andrei Iosivas is expected to miss four to six weeks because of a thumb injury, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：ベンガルズのアンドレイ・イオスィヴァスは4〜6週間の離脱見込み
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNが情報筋から得た情報によると、ベンガルズのワイドレシーバー（WR）アンドレイ・イオスィヴァスは親指の負傷により4〜6週間離脱する見込み。
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Andrei Iosivas is expected to miss four to six weeks because of a thumb injury, sources told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

Iosivas will be placed on injured reserve after undergoing surgery Wednesday to repair the injury, which he suffered in Cincinnati's Week 2 victory against the Houston Texans.

Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Iosivas will be eligible to return at some point this season. With the IR designation, he will miss a minimum of four games.

Iosivas had been Cincinnati's third starting wide receiver. Through the first two games of the season, he had three catches on four targets for 19 yards.

Taylor said the Bengals (2-0) will have varied options to replace Iosivas until he returns.

"[We have] several guys that can step up, whether it's in the receiver room, tight end room, there's a lot of ways we're going to fill that," Taylor said Wednesday.

It's unclear when Iosivas suffered the injury. The fourth-year receiver had one catch for 7 yards in the 20-6 victory against the Texans. His final play was in punt coverage with 2:16 left in the game.

Cincinnati will have one available spot on the 53-player active roster. Taylor didn't specify how the Bengals will use that opening. Cincinnati has six wide receivers on the roster, including Ke'Shawn Williams, who has been inactive on game days for the first two weeks of the season.

The Bengals play the rival Pittsburgh Steelers (1-1) on Sunday and are looking to go 3-0 for the first time since 2015.

articles.headline: Former NFL star Antonio Brown to accept plea deal, avoid prison
articles.description: Former NFL star Antonio Brown will accept a plea deal in his second-degree attempted murder case, resulting in probation, his attorney said.
articles.headlineJa: 元NFLスターのアントニオ・ブラウン、司法取引に応じ刑務所行きを回避へ
articles.descriptionJa: 元NFLスターのアントニオ・ブラウンが第2級殺人未遂事件で司法取引に応じ、執行猶予処分となる予定だと彼の弁護士が明かした。
articles.body:
Former NFL star Antonio Brown will accept a plea deal in his second-degree attempted murder case, resulting in probation and avoiding the possibility of a decades-long prison sentence, his attorney said Wednesday.

The deal comes two weeks after Brown's accuser -- the sole alleged victim in the case -- announced that he would no longer participate in Brown's prosecution.

"They made [Brown] an offer he couldn't refuse," Brown's attorney, Mark Eiglarsh, said in a statement. "There is a profound difference between believing you can win a case and deciding that you and your family cannot afford to spend another year, or potentially several years, wearing an ankle monitor and fighting it."

Brown will appear before a judge in one week to formally accept the deal, which will be a reduced charge of aggravated assault, Eiglarsh told ESPN on Wednesday.

"There's no prison, there's no jail, there's no house arrest. There's only straight probation," Eiglarsh told ESPN. "And no alcohol or drug evaluation, no psychological evaluation, no letter of apology, no community service hours, no fines. Just stay away from the victim.

"No one in their right mind will continue with litigation and/or uncertain stand your ground and trial when [the prosecutors] threw that on the table."

Brown, 38, faced up to 30 years in prison if convicted, with a mandatory minimum of 20 years under Florida law, for an incident involving gunfire outside an amateur boxing match in Miami's Little Haiti neighborhood in May 2025. He pleaded not guilty in November 2025 and filed a motion to dismiss the following month based on Florida's "stand your ground" law.

Eiglarsh added that Brown's decision to accept the deal "should not be interpreted as a retreat from his position that he acted lawfully."

The alleged victim, Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu, said through his attorney on Sept. 9 that "he does not wish to participate" in Brown's prosecution. Attorney Richard L. Cooper said earlier this month that Nantambu forgave Brown for the May 2025 incident.

"We believe that the ends of justice are accomplished with this plea deal, and my client wishes Mr. Brown good health," Cooper told ESPN on Wednesday.

After the May 2025 incident, Brown spent nearly six months in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, where he traveled after the incident, before being extradited by U.S. marshals. Brown was released on $25,000 bail and placed on house arrest with a GPS ankle monitor.

According to the "stand your ground" motion, Brown was trying to get to his car for safety after Nantambu had attacked him. Police said Brown punched Nantambu in the face and, along with two others, continued the attack.

Nantambu walked away, according to a police description of the security footage. Brown then "chases him down with a gun and shoots at him at point-blank range," according to a prosecutor. articles.headline: Inside the basketball of 'One Tree Hill' 23 years later
articles.description: In honor of 23 years since "One Tree Hill" premiered, James Lafferty & Co. take us inside the basketball heart of the cult classic TV show.
articles.headlineJa: 23年後の『One Tree Hill』におけるバスケットボールの舞台裏
articles.descriptionJa: 『One Tree Hill』の放送開始から23年を記念し、ジェームズ・ラファティらがこのカルト的人気ドラマの核心であるバスケットボールの裏側を明かす。
articles.body:
WILMINGTON, N.C. -- "Are you here for the big game?" my new friend behind the car rental counter asked shortly after I touched down in Michael Jordan's hometown.

"People are saying you need to be in line by 7 a.m. if you want a chance at a decent seat," she exclaimed before I could answer.

To my surprise, my big game and her big game were one and the same: the "Hey 23" basketball game celebrating 23 years since the hit television show "One Tree Hill" first aired.

Pausing to look around Wilmington International Airport, it appeared nearly everyone arriving in town had the same purpose. Couples, families and groups of friends of all ages -- all donning black, white and royal blue, and not of the Duke Blue Devils variety.

I had counted at least seven combined "Scott" jerseys and two red Quentin Fields-inspired capes before a handmade "You can't kill Dan Scott" sign diverted my attention.

Then the same cheerful voice snapped me back into focus.

"Your car is ready. Just head to spot No. 23! See you tomorrow!"

Unclear whether my rental assignment was intentional or an omen, I grabbed the keys and stepped out into the North Carolina heat.

If a 23rd anniversary feels arbitrary, you're clearly not a "One Tree Hill" fan.

OTH's premise centered around a pair of half-brothers, Lucas (played by Chad Michael Murray) and Nathan Scott (played by James Lafferty) who starred on their high school basketball team in the fictional North Carolina small town of Tree Hill.

The beloved teen drama -- and in my entirely unbiased opinion, the most slept-on basketball show of our generation -- followed Nathan Scott, aka No. 23 and his journey from winning a state championship in high school to being recruited by Duke until his college plans were derailed by his involvement in a point-shaving scheme. Scott eventually went on to win a national title at Maryland before suffering a spinal injury the night before the NBA draft. He then mounted a comeback that started with SlamBall, then saw him play in the D-League and finally become the starting point guard for the then-Charlotte Bobcats.

In the 2000s, Nathan's evolution from a brash high school standout to a selfless NBA star left an indelible mark on a generation of fans. The Ravens never existed -- there was no Tree Hill High and no state championship banner. But for the people who watched the scripted show and the actors who portrayed the characters, the basketball was real. In the years since its historic nine-season run from 2003 to '12, it has amassed a cult following of a magnitude I couldn't quite grasp until setting foot where the show was filmed.

'Hey 23'

On Sept. 19, in front of nearly 5,000 fans at UNC Wilmington's Trask Coliseum, the show's stars, including Lafferty, Murray, Antwon Tanner, Robbie Jones, Bryan Greenberg and Stephen Colletti took the court together again.

articles.headline: Falcons hoping Penix's return sparks their offense as they visit the Packers
articles.description: — Michael Penix Jr.'s return comes at a time when the
articles.headlineJa: ファルコンズ、パッカーズ戦でペニックスの復帰がオフェンスの起爆剤となることを期待
articles.descriptionJa: マイケル・ペニックス・ジュニアの復帰は、チームが…
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- — Michael Penix Jr.'s return comes at a time when the winless Atlanta Falcons need someone to provide a jolt for their lifeless offense.


              Atlanta’s offense couldn’t reach the red zone as the Falcons opened the season with losses to the Pittsburgh Steelers and Carolina Panthers. The Falcons were the first team since the Rams in 2008 not to run any plays from inside an opponent’s 20-yard line through the first two games of a season.


              Penix now is back from a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee. The 26-year-old quarterback is ready to play his first game since Nov. 16 on Thursday night as the Falcons visit the Green Bay Packers.


              “I’ve been working extremely hard to get to this point,” Penix said. “Man, this has been a long journey.”


              Atlanta (0-2) needs the boost that Penix will try to provide.


              Cooper Rush and Jack Strand threw a combined five interceptions with one touchdown pass — a 23-yarder from Rush to Bijan Robinson in Week 1 — while Penix worked his way back.


              The Packers expect to face a more capable Atlanta offense now that Penix is back.


              “He’s a quarterback that’s gone in there and played really solid football,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said. “So I would bet that their offense is going to look a little bit different Thursday night.”


              Green Bay (1-1) has concerns of its own.


              All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons is recovering from a torn ACL and running back Josh Jacobs remains on the commissioner’s exempt list. Wide receiver Jayden Reed and offensive tackle Zach Bako-Bewele were carted off the field during the Packers’ 20-17 overtime victory over the New York Jets on Sunday.


              Bako-Bewele tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season. Reed’s potential return from a neck injury is unknown.


              The injury to Bako-Bewele creates more adversity for an offensive line that hasn’t established a rhythm yet. Left guard Aaron Banks injured his toe against the Jets, leaving his status for Thursday’s game uncertain.


              Packers quarterback Jordan Love says all those injuries up front shouldn’t change the expectations.


              “I expect those guys to go out there and put their best foot forward and give me time to be able to go out there and try dicing a defense up,” Love said. “That’s the expectations, whoever’s out there. Nothing changes.”

articles.headline: NBA Rank 2026, players Nos. 50-11: Where LeBron, Steph, KD check in
articles.description: Our countdown of the NBA's top 100 players continues. See which stars just missed a spot in the top 10 -- and where three legends land.
articles.headlineJa: NBAランキング2026（50位〜11位）：レブロン、ステフ、KDは何位にランクインしたか
articles.descriptionJa: NBAトップ100選手のカウントダウンは続きます。トップ10入りを惜しくも逃したスター選手たちや、3人のレジェンドが何位にランクインしたかをご覧ください。
articles.body:
NBA Rank is back! With less than one month until opening night, let's continue counting down the league's best players for 2026-27.

After unveiling players Nos. 100-51 on Tuesday, our rankings now enter the top 50. It's a group headlined by former MVPs, future first-ballot Hall of Famers and young stars expected to take major leaps this season.  

It's also where LeBron James checks in, his first time outside the top 10 in NBA Rank's 15-year history. (You can jump to LeBron's NBA Rank here.)

The rankings rollout concludes Thursday with our expert panel's top 10 players. And that panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition.

In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list. That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list, which features plenty of superstars who just missed our top 10.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

50. Dylan Harper

G | San Antonio Spurs

Age: 20

2025 NBA Rank: NR

The youngest member of the Spurs was the one who seemed to rise highest in the altitude of the Finals and stands to make a big jump in Year 2, whether he stays coming off the bench or makes the leap to the first five. He will earn more respect from the officials (1.7 free throw attempts in 69 games as a rookie), take a bigger role in the offense and improve on his already-respectable playmaking. Harper is an All-Star in the making. -- Vincent Goodwill

Signature stat: Harper had six games with at least 15 points and 65% shooting from the field in the 2026 playoffs, the most by a guard in NBA postseason history.

Fantasy projection: 15.2 PTS, 5.0 AST, 4.4 REB

49. Lauri Markkanen

F | Utah Jazz

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 43

Markkanen, a scoring forward who can stretch the court, has languished as a forgotten man in Utah. The Finnish star's competence often came into conflict with the Jazz's desire to improve their draft positioning during a multiyear rebuilding effort, and he has appeared in only one game in April over the past four seasons. Though his contract is overly generous for a player lacking All-NBA credentials, Markkanen should benefit from Utah's recent talent upgrades as he eyes his first career postseason appearance. -- Ben Golliver

Signature stat: Markkanen has nine seasons with at least 100 3-pointers, tied with Karl-Anthony Towns and Dirk Nowitzki for the most by a 7-footer in NBA history.

Fantasy projection: 23.8 PTS, 7.2 REB, 1.9 AST

articles.headline: Man United selling chunks of Old Trafford pitch
articles.description: Old Trafford -- the home of Manchester United -- has seen plenty of history over the years. Now, fans can own a piece of the pitch ...for £125 ($165).
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッド、オールド・トラッフォードのピッチの芝生を小分け販売
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの本拠地オールド・トラッフォードは、長年にわたり数々の歴史を刻んできた。そして今、ファンは125ポンド（約165ドル）でピッチの一部を手に入れることができる。
articles.body:
Old Trafford -- the home of Manchester United -- has seen plenty of history over the years. Now, fans can own a piece of the pitch ...for £125 ($165). 

The hallowed stadium has witnessed countless victories -- particularly during the Sir Alex Ferguson era, in which United won 13 Premier League titles and two Champions League trophies, and numerous FA Cup triumphs.

The club is selling chunks of the ground off. 

Old Trafford has borne witness to some of United's worst moments, too, including a 5-0 defeat to bitter rivals Liverpool, a 6-1 loss to Tottenham and, most recently, a capitulation against Brighton in the Carabao Cup -- in which the Red Devils let a 2-0 lead slip and fell to a 3-2 defeat. 

The loss to Brighton marked the first time in 42 years that United had lost a match at home when leading at half-time.

According to club media, the pitch was completely dug up and stripped back to its foundation in June -- for the first time in 14 years -- and sections of it were preserved and then placed into glass cubes.

On their website, United said the digging up of the pitch was completed by groundsperson Tony Sinclair and was done to regrow the surface in order to "improve player welfare and water drainage."

United fans may be hoping that their season will soon improve along with the pitch.

articles.headline: Napoli president wants ultras out of any new stadium, warns Allegri
articles.description: With two Serie A trophies in the last four years and five other domestic cups, Napoli president Aurelio De Laurentiis is proud of what he has accomplished since rescuing the club from bankruptcy and starting in Serie C more than two decades ago.
articles.headlineJa: ナポリ会長、新スタジアムからのウルトラス排除を望む＆アッレグリに警告
articles.descriptionJa: 過去4年間で2度のセリエA優勝と5度の国内カップ戦制覇を果たしたナポリのアウレリオ・デ・ラウレンティス会長は、20年以上前にクラブを破産から救いセリエCから再スタートして以降達成してきた功績に誇りを持っている。
articles.body:
With two Serie A trophies in the last four years and five other domestic cups, Napoli president Aurelio De Laurentiis is proud of what he has accomplished since rescuing the club from bankruptcy and starting in Serie C more than two decades ago.

Yet he also wants more.

De Laurentiis discussed plans for a new stadium that he hopes would be more attractive to families by keeping out hard-core "ultra" fans and sent a warning to coach Massimiliano Allegri while collecting an award recognizing his career in sports at the Foreign Press Association on Wednesday.

A film producer, De Laurentiis is one of the last Italian owners of Serie A's biggest clubs. Napoli currently play in the dilapidated Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, which is owned by the city and where sight lines are poor due to a running track.

"I have a letter of intent signed a month ago by which in eastern Naples we've found 38 hectares (94 acres) where I've planned a 70,000-seat stadium with 120 sky boxes, plus restaurants and an interactive museum," De Laurentiis said.

However, city officials have proposed renovating the Maradona stadium in time for the 2032 European Championship that Italy are co-hosting with Turkey.

De Laurentiis has had issues with the "ultras" for years and most recently made an attempt to prevent the hard-core supporters from bringing banners inside the stadium.

"Soccer should be about passion and participation. It has to be educational for kids. You can't have hooligans ... or 'ultras' that are moulded from the Mafia, 'ndrangheta and Camorra," De Laurentiis said, listing three of Italy's organized crime syndicates.

"Until our police chiefs and government ministers get the situation under control it's a major problem."

Despite the recent success, De Laurentiis has employed five different coaches since Luciano Spalletti left after leading Napoli to the Serie A title in 2023 -- their first championship since the days when Diego Maradona played for the club more than three decades earlier.

De Laurentiis was asked about Spalletti and his response could be interpreted as a warning to Allegri, Napoli's current coach, too.

Allegri is already under pressure after Napoli has won only two of six matches since he was hired to replace the departed Antonio Conte.

"Coaches need to understand that they are workers hired to direct an orchestra of footballers," said De Laurentiis, who often clashes with his coaches. "But they're still employees. Sometimes they forget that."

Despite being Serie A champion at the time, Napoli didn't qualify for the 2025 Club World Cup. And De Laurentiis doesn't sound very enthusiastic about the possibility of his club playing in the 2029 edition, either, citing too many matches.

Chelsea, who won the Club World Cup, and finalist Paris Saint-Germain played 64 and 65 matches, respectively, that season.
